subject: Post-demo: OptiServe lab proposal — p95/p99 & tokens/sec benchmark
messages:
From: Tim Holt <tim.holt@optiserve.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jennifer Park <jennifer.park@optiserve.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — next steps for inference perf comparison

Rachel — thanks for the demo today. Quick notes from our side and what we need to decide before the lab: 

- High level ask: can Redwood run an apples-to-apples perf comparison vs the hyperscaler we currently use (MegaCloud AI)? We care about p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec (sustained throughput).
- Scope: please include our top 3 prompt families (customer support, summarization, short Q&A). We can provide anonymized samples.
- Environment: is it better for you to run Redwood-hosted tests or inside our AWS account (we prefer to avoid moving any real traffic outside our VPC)?
- Compliance: Jennifer (cc) will need SOC2 evidence and a short list of logs you will collect during tests.
- Timeline: we’d like an initial run next week if possible. Also, rough cost for the bench run would be helpful.

Thanks — Tim

Tim Holt
Head of AI Engineering, OptiServe
Tim.Holt@optiserve.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tim Holt <tim.holt@optiserve.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — next steps for inference perf comparison

Hi Tim — great to talk yesterday, and thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise lab proposal so we have alignment before we schedule execution. I’ve attached a one-page bench plan (optiserve_bench_plan_v1.xlsx) and a small sample prompts bundle.

Recap / goals
- Primary metrics: p95 latency, p99 latency, median latency, sustained tokens/sec (measured as tokens generated per second across sustained window), error rate (5xx/4xx), and cost per 1M tokens for the measured configs.
- Comparators: Redwood (redwood-m2-8k quantized) vs MegaCloud AI (their production text endpoint). We’ll run identical prompt workloads.

Proposed test matrix (initial run)
1) Single-user latency profile — 100 sequential requests using each prompt family, cold start measured separately.
2) Sustained throughput probe — concurrency sweep at 1, 4, 8, 16 simultaneous sessions; measure steady-state tokens/sec over 10-minute windows.
3) p95/p99 tail analysis — capture per-request latencies and plot distributions; include 95th/99th percentiles pre/post caching.

Measurement details (high level)
- Warmup: 200 requests per model before measurement window to fill KV caches.
- Token counting: use tokenizer-match method (we’ll provide tokenizer script).
- Batching: run both single-token streaming and batched request scenarios.
- Environment: we can run Redwood-hosted tests to avoid networking setup, but if you prefer we can run in your AWS VPC via temporary infra (requires a short infra playbook). Please indicate preference.

What we need from you
- Anonymized prompt samples (JSONL) for the three families (redact PII).
- A small representative traffic trace for concurrency profile (if you want us to emulate live traffic).
- Confirmation on whether you want Redwood-hosted or VPC-run tests.

Proposed timeline
- Confirm artifacts by Fri 2027-09-03
- Kickoff & infra decision by Mon 2027-09-06
- Initial run (sanity + latency) by Wed–Thu 2027-09-08–09

Next steps (action items)
- Tim: send samples + prefered infra option.
- Jennifer: list of required compliance artifacts (SOC2 fields you expect to verify).
- Ben/Neha/Aditya: internal owners for run — we’ll coordinate the infra and measurement scripts.

If that looks good I’ll schedule a 30m kickoff and send a compact runbook.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Exec — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tim Holt <tim.holt@optiserve.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — next steps for inference perf comparison

On Thu, Sep 2, 2027 at 10:05 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Recap / goals
> - Primary metrics: p95 latency, p99 latency, median latency, sustained tokens/sec ...

Quick technical notes from my side to make sure the bench is rigorous: 
- Warmup: agree on 200 requests but we should also include a separate cold-start bucket (empty cache) for 50 requests to capture first-request inflation.
- Concurrency & batching: when sweeping concurrency, we will run with and without our continuous batching layer enabled to show its impact. Please confirm whether you want batching on the hyperscaler side (if their API supports it).
- Measurement script: we’ll provide rdw_measurement_script.sh (stub attached) that logs per-request timestamps + token counts to a Parquet file. That file will be used to compute exact p95/p99.
- Time sync: if you run in your VPC, ensure NTP is correct; we’ll include a UTC-marker event to align logs.
- Cost calc: we’ll capture raw model token counts and attach our unit-cost model (cost per 1M tokens) so you can compare realized unit economics.

Ben
Ben Carter
Inference Performance Lead, Redwood
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tim Holt <tim.holt@optiserve.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks — next steps for inference perf comparison

Tim — quick security/compliance notes so Jennifer has context: 
- SOC2: for a short bench we can provide the control mapping and the audit logs we capture during the run (request/response metadata, model version, timestamp). We will not retain prompt content beyond the bench unless you direct us to.
- Data handling: we recommend you provide anonymized samples; if any sensitive data is unavoidable we can run inside your VPC and use ephemeral keys.
- KMS/Audit: if we run on Redwood-hosted infra we will provide per-request trace IDs and a signed digest of logs for audit.

Attachments included: sample_prompts.json (anonymized examples), SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf (stub).

Neha Kapoor
Dir, Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

- We will anonymize and deliver the three JSONL prompt families by EOD Fri 2027-09-03 (we’ll drop them to the secure S3 bucket you shared).
- OptiServe prefers Redwood-hosted initial run — we can revisit VPC execution for the final validation if needed.
- Cost: we’d like a ballpark estimate for the full lab (including the throughput sweep). Can you send a short pricing note?
- Kickoff: Mon 2027-09-06 at 10:00 AM PT works for our infra folks. Please send calendar invite.

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/OPT-2081

I’ll also share Jennifer’s list of SOC2 fields this afternoon. Looking forward to the run.

—Tim
